narration.full_text: Namaste students! We're diving into the algebraic method of solving pairs of linear equations, specifically focusing on the substitution method. This technique is incredibly useful for finding the values of variables that satisfy both equations simultaneously. By the end of this section, you'll not only understand the steps involved but also be able to confidently apply this method to various problems, including real-world scenarios. The substitution method involves expressing one variable in terms of the other from one equation, and then substituting that expression into the second equation. This transforms the system into a single equation with one variable, which is much easier to solve. Once you find the value of one variable, you can easily find the other. Let's look at a simple example to illustrate this. Imagine we have a situation where we know the age of a son and his father, and we want to verify these ages using a system of equations. For instance, if the age of the son is 10 years and the age of the father is 40 years, we can represent this relationship algebraically. This method is particularly effective when one of the equations can be easily rearranged to isolate a variable. Remember, practice is key to mastering this technique, so pay close attention to the steps as we go through them.

visual_beats.description: Key steps of Substitution Method: 1. Express one variable in terms of another. 2. Substitute into the second equation.
Result: Single equation with one variable. Solve for one variable, then find the other.
Example: Age problem. Age of the son = 10 years. Age of the father = 40 years.
Tip: Choose equations where a variable is easily isolated. Practice is essential!
